failures.evidence: The line reads: "A claim brings a person's answers, comments and messages; otherwise, `dispatch issue-update --route session:<your id>` (`--route ''` on release) or `envoy_subscribe notifications.dispatch.issue.<KEY>.>`. Never route such an issue." (1) 'otherwise' can be read as 'without a claim', which is false. At this head, on a claimed issue, an agent's comment and a targeted message reach the claimant on no agent topic (live cases agent-comment {} and targeted-message {}). So a claimant still needs the subscription or the route for anything a claim does not bring. The architect's 'without a claim' wording would be false for the same reason. (2) 'such an issue' has no antecedent in its own paragraph. Its intended noun, an issue with the `legion` label, or under one, is the last clause of the paragraph before. Inside a paragraph about the agent's own claimed issue it reads as 'never route the issue you claimed', contradicting the routing instruction just before it. Corrected text, measured to keep the three Dispatch skills at 1997 words (`find skills/dispatch skills/dispatch-first skills/dispatch-writing-specs -type f | xargs cat | wc -w`; the guard in packages/pi-envoy/src/skills-guard.test.ts requires fewer than 2,000; it is 1998 now): line 46 ends 'Never write the status of, or route, an issue with the `legion` label, or under one.' and line 48 becomes 'A claim brings a person's answers, comments and messages; for anything else, `dispatch issue-update --route session:<your id>` (`--route ''` on release) or `envoy_subscribe notifications.dispatch.issue.<KEY>.>`.' No red test was written: a test asserting the skill's wording is a source-text test, which the repository's test rules forbid.
